events.title: Colossus computer operational at Bletchley Park
events.summary: The first Colossus computer became operational at Bletchley Park on February 5, 1944 — an electronic code-breaking machine built to decrypt German Lorenz teleprinter traffic.
events.about: Colossus used thousands of vacuum tubes and programmable logic to analyze ciphertext at speeds impossible for human clerks. Tommy Flowers designed it in secret; ten Colossus machines ran by war's end — a landmark in electronic digital computing kept classified until the 1970s.

narrative.whyChosen: Colossus was among the first electronic digital computers used in production.
narrative.whyImportant: It demonstrated large-scale programmable electronics for real-time cryptanalysis.
narrative.problemSolved: Allied intelligence needed to break high-volume encrypted teleprinter messages faster than manual methods.
